proposed_fixes.title: Keep FancyZones zone visibility consistent after Shift-drag release
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis only: the shift/drag state transition may leave the overlay hidden or the drag state stale after a Shift-drag ends; the current report does not establish which transition fails.
plan: Reproduce with the current reported build, record the FancyZones shift-drag setting, and trace FancyZones::OnKeyboardInput, DraggingState::SetShiftState, UpdateDraggingState, and zone-overlay visibility through Shift-down, Shift-up, mouse release, and the next drag.
Do not repeat the existing drag-start GetAsyncKeyState resynchronization change; first establish whether the failed state is a missing key-up, drag-end cleanup, or an overlay visibility transition.
If a state remains inconsistent after a reproduced transition, correct that specific transition and add a focused regression test for Shift-up/drag-end followed by another drag.
verification: Repeat the issue sequence and confirm the zones remain available after releasing Shift and the mouse button.
Perform another drag without toggling FancyZones; confirm normal zone display and snapping continue.

confidence.rationale: The behavior and affected state machine are supported by the report and source, but no trace confirms which event or overlay transition fails. Related issue #29257 already fixed a different stale Shift state at drag start.

issue_context.summary: Holding Shift during a FancyZones window drag hides the zone overlay, and toggling FancyZones is the only reported way to restore it.
known_information: The reporter uses PowerToys v0.101.2362 on Windows 11 and identifies FancyZones.
Dragging a window onto a zone while holding Shift makes zones disappear; toggling FancyZones off and on restores them temporarily.
The author reattached the diagnostic ZIP in a comment after an automated triage reply reported the archive could not be analyzed; this artifact does not copy diagnostic contents.
The author’s attachment reply is the latest activity, and Needs-Team-Response is set.
inferences: The inability to show zones again may involve a stale shift/drag or overlay visibility state, but the report does not identify the exact transition.

Existing closed issue #29257 concerned intermittent Shift-key failures and has a committed drag-start Shift-state resync in current source; the current Shift-drag overlay symptom may be different and is not established as covered.
issue_context.analysis: The new report is specific enough for a maintainer-side reproduction. The current FancyZones state machine combines Shift and secondary-mouse state to compute dragging, while Shift transitions arrive through the raw-input path. Prior code history already addressed stale Shift state at drag start; any new proposal should trace mid-drag and cleanup transitions instead of duplicating that fix.
initial_investigation: At upstream commit 1b33221dfa19f30d71409eb550807883fb27283a, src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesLib/DraggingState.cpp::Enable, SetShiftState, and UpdateDraggingState seed Shift at drag start, accept raw-input updates, and derive dragging from Shift XOR secondary-mouse state.

Closed issue #29257 (https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/29257) has Resolution-Fix Committed and a fix in current source that re-seeds Shift at drag start for stale transitions after RDP/wake/unlock. Its reported symptom was intermittent Shift-key failure/phantom zones, not this post-Shift-drag overlay loss; treat it as related context, not proof that #51237 is fixed.
No cross-reference to an upstream PR and no matching MuyuanMS issue, PR, or branch was found for #51237.

reproduce.title: Verify FancyZones remains available after Shift-drag
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.101.2362 or current supported stable build
prerequisites: Use a simple two-zone layout on one monitor.
Record the current Shift-drag setting before testing.
setup: Use an ordinary resizable window and keep the same monitor/layout for each run.
steps: Begin dragging the window toward a FancyZone while holding Shift.
Move it over a visible zone, then release Shift and the mouse button.
Observe whether the zone overlay remains available for another drag.
Repeat the next drag without toggling FancyZones; if the overlay disappears, trace Shift state, drag state, and overlay visibility through key-up and drag-end.
reproduce.expected_result: Zones remain available after the Shift-drag ends, and a subsequent drag works without disabling and re-enabling FancyZones.
